items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: he started giving special lessons for his class violin player. So he gave me about a dozen lessons, private you see.

ctx.x: There were some good musicians around in Virginia. I know that a lot of them, one fellow made a name for himself, went to New York, named Ward Pinkett but he died. I think he went to Hampton Institute. Yeah. I doubt if you'd known him, he's probably younger than you. We had an Italian professor up there, he was good. Professor Gadibasio was his name.

Gadibasio. Gadibasio was his name. And he was fun. We had a crack brass band up there. Oh yeah? Crack brass band up there. Readin'? Fakin'? Sure, I don't know fakin'. All readin'? You had to read all readin'. There was no fakin' in that. What about the brass band here?

What's the name of it? Promo Brass Band. Promo. All of those were readers too. That was all readin', your father and everybody. Every one of them were readers, good readers too. Who was in that band? We didn't get that either I don't think.
